subject: Immediate: HelixCommerce throughput degradation — hosted API p95/p99 regressions
messages:
From: Paul Gill <paul.gill@helixcommerce.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: ops@helixcommerce.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 22:05:00 -0700
Subject: Something broke — generation throughput down across our busiest routes

Hi Priyom,

We started seeing a pronounced drop in tokens/sec for our production calls to /v1/generate around 21:40 PDT. p95 and p99 latency are spiking and a few customers are timing out. This appears to be across our EU and US traffic — we routed ~10% to EU yesterday as part of our testing.

Attached is a screenshot of our internal Grafana alert (alerts firing for spikes on p99). Our ops team has rolled back nothing on our side; this looks like it could be on your hosted API. Can you confirm whether any platform change went out in the 21:00-21:45 PDT window? We need visibility ASAP — this is customer-impacting (3 active customers reported).

Paul
Head of Platform, HelixCommerce
paul.gill@helixcommerce.com

-----
Attachment: helix_incident_screenshot.png (PNG, 320KB)
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Paul Gill <paul.gill@helixcommerce.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 22:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Something broke — generation throughput down across our busiest routes

Hi Paul — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We're investigating now and I've looped in SRE and engineering. Quick answers while we dig in:
- I don't see any customer-targeted config changes from Helix on our side.
- We did have a staged rollout earlier tonight (20:55 PDT) of a quantization profile and a kernel-selector tweak intended to reduce cost for long-context models. The rollout was supposed to be canaryed.

I'm escalating to our on-call and product lead. We'll update within 30 minutes with what we find and next steps (rollback vs mitigations).

Respectfully,
Priyom Das
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 22:34:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Something broke — generation throughput down across our busiest routes

Team — initial triage notes from runtime and metrics:
- Correlation: p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec drop coincide with a canary rollout of quant_profile:v3 + kernel-selector v2 at 20:55 PDT.
- Metrics: observed ~40% drop in token/s on the affected nodes (model-family: rwd-open-13B, seq-len: 1024). p99 latency jumped from ~480ms to ~1.4s on requests to that model-family.
- Errors: increased 429s and a small uptick in 504s linked to backend queuing. No OOMs detected.
- Canary scope: ~7% of hosted capacity, but traffic distribution caused Helix to hit canary nodes disproportionately because of their region affinity.

Actionable next steps proposed:
1) Immediately remove quant_profile:v3 from canary hosts (roll back to v2) — low-risk and reversible.
2) Force kernel-selector to the previous stable branch for rwd-open-13B for hosted API traffic serving Helix.
3) Open a short-service incident channel and notify Helix execs.

I'll prepare logs and a short dashboard link. If we don't see <15% degradation within 15 minutes after rollback, escalate to full rollback of the canary pipeline.

-rishi
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 22:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Something broke — generation throughput down across our busiest routes

Data point from runtime profiler and KV cache traces:
- Quant_profile:v3 uses a different per-layer scaling for int8 paths; that changes kernel invocation patterns and increases the number of kernel launches for short batches. This raises per-token overhead by ~10-20% per call on those nodes, and when combined with our micro-batching heuristics at low concurrency it explains the throughput slump.
- Kernel-selector v2 changed the fallback order for native GEMM kernels; on Ampere nodes some workloads pick a slower but numerically preferable kernel.

Given this, I recommend:
- Rollback quant_profile:v3 from the canary set immediately (we can re-run with modified micro-batching hints).
- Pin kernel-selector to the stable strategy for affected instance-types for now.
- Throttle Helix traffic away from affected canary hosts via routing override while rollback completes.

I'll start the rollback runbook now (refer to Redwood runbook section 4.2). Attaching the runbook excerpt.

-Aditya
Sr. Software Engineer, Runtime
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 23:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Something broke — generation throughput down across our busiest routes

Team — thank you for the quick triage. Priyom, please send Helix an executive escalation note summarizing: impact, what we changed, ETA for rollback and monitoring confirmation, and any immediate credit/compensation offers.

Paul — from Redwood's side we will:
- Rollback quant_profile:v3 on canary hosts now and pin kernel-selector to stable for affected instance types.
- Reroute 100% of Helix traffic off canaries during the window.
- Monitor p95/p99 and tokens/sec and update you at 15-minute intervals until stabilized.

We understand the customer impact and will expedite. Priyom, put the credit ask on my radar and loop in finance if Helix requests formal compensation.

Laura Bennett
VP, Sales & Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Paul Gill <paul.gill@helixcommerce.com>, ops@helixcommerce.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 00:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood update: immediate rollback started (Helix impact mitigation)

Paul — quick executive summary for your leadership team: 
- Impact: We observed a Helix-facing increase in p95/p99 latency and ~40% tokens/sec decrease starting ~20:55 PDT during a canary rollout of a new quantization profile and kernel ordering change. A small number of Helix customers reported timeouts.
- What we changed: Initiated rollback of quant_profile:v3 on canaries at 23:05 PDT and pinned kernel-selector to stable branch for rwd-open-13B. We also temporarily routed Helix traffic away from canary pool.
- ETA & next checks: Rollback is in progress; we will report p95/p99 and tokens/sec at: 23:20, 23:35, and 23:50 PDT.
- Attachments: runbook excerpt and an incident screenshot from your alert.

We recognize the severity and will coordinate a post-incident summary that includes root cause analysis and a plan to avoid regressing on token/s overhead (including tuning micro-batching heuristics and revalidating quant profile performance on Ampere hardware).

If Helix would like an emergency call with engineering and SRE, we can arrange that now.

Thanks for raising this quickly — we'll keep you updated.

Priyom Das
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 01:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood update: immediate rollback started (Helix impact mitigation)

Update after rollback:
- Timeline: rollback completed by 00:30 PDT.
- Metrics: tokens/sec for Helix routes recovered to within 8% of baseline; p95/p99 returned to pre-canary ranges (p99 ~520ms).
- Next steps: run a targeted perf validation for quant_profile:v3 on a mirrored load that represents Helix traffic before re-enabling.

I'll prepare a short post-incident summary (RCA + mitigation plan) and share by end of day. If Helix needs an on-call deep dive, we can schedule a 30-minute review.

-rishi
SRE, Redwood Inference
